first.rationale: Promotional pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMBs and has prior evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. Verify its customer quality and post-promotion economics, while checking onboarding evidence as the strongest alternative. Keep the test guarded because durable retention and downstream value are not established in the consolidated pricing memory.

mid.rationale: Choose shortened onboarding because it directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has verified gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, aligning with sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing: although it lifted signups and qualified revenue initially, 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive its first renewal cycle. A standard experiment validates impact in the current environment before broader rollout.

final2.rationale: Continue with shortened onboarding. It directly addresses the current completion decline and has verified improvements in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. The competitor escalation increases pressure to discount, but the verified pricing experiment reduced 30-day retention by 12% and failed at first renewal, making it incompatible with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Run a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout because current-market impact still needs validation.
